days.thesis: Agent workflows become graphs when the product needs explicit transition authority; the important decision is what is allowed to happen after a node completes.
days.target_reader: AI product leaders designing reliable multi-agent workflows
days.reader_problem: AI product leaders need a reliable decision about which workflow transition may execute after each agent completes.
days.product_decision: Define allowed transitions, conditional edges, and terminal states before adding more agents.
days.authority_statement: Connect graph structure to the product authority that permits the next workflow action.
days.why_now: Current ADK and AutoGen documentation now make deterministic, conditional, looping, and graph execution explicit product surfaces.
days.dominant_take: Framework documentation explains graph primitives and orchestration patterns.
days.missing_angle: The product decision is not whether to draw a graph; it is who or what has authority to select the next edge.
days.artifact_policy: Return DIAGRAM with two or three nodes showing node completion, edge-policy evaluation, and the permitted next action. Do not use a carousel.

evidence.title: Google ADK template agent workflows
evidence.claim: Google ADK describes workflow agents as components that control how and when sub-agents run. Its predefined sequential, loop, and parallel patterns use deterministic logic rather than consulting a model for orchestration; ADK 2.0 points to graph-based and dynamic workflows for more control.
evidence.caveats: The page exposes a 2026 copyright but no publication date; accessed 2026-08-09.

evidence.title: Microsoft AutoGen GraphFlow workflows
evidence.claim: AutoGen GraphFlow follows a directed graph for strict execution control. Edges define allowed paths and may be conditional; the documentation recommends graphs when different outcomes need different next steps, while warning that GraphFlow is experimental.
evidence.caveats: GraphFlow is explicitly experimental and may change.

evidence.title: Production Engineering OS V2 stage machine
evidence.claim: Abhillash's public Production Engineering OS advances a declared stage machine only through admitted artifacts or engine-owned actions, appends digest-bound events to an evidence ledger, and resumes from a single persisted run-state document rather than reconstructing authority from chat.
evidence.caveats: Author-owned public repository evidence; this establishes implementation design, not third-party adoption.

days.thesis: A runtime budget is incomplete unless the product defines what happens when the budget is exhausted before the job is done.
days.target_reader: AI product leaders operating long-running autonomous agents
days.reader_problem: AI product leaders need a reliable decision for unfinished work when an autonomous agent exhausts its runtime budget.
days.product_decision: Specify the exhausted state, preserved state, continuation authority, and user-visible recovery path with every budget.
days.authority_statement: Turn token caps into an explicit unfinished-work and recovery contract.
days.why_now: Google added documented Managed Agents token-budget controls and a resumable incomplete state in July 2026.
days.dominant_take: The launch is described primarily as cost control for autonomous loops.
days.missing_angle: The more consequential product surface is the state transition at exhaustion and who may grant a fresh budget.
days.artifact_policy: Text-only is acceptable. Return NONE unless a visual materially clarifies the exhausted-to-resume state transition.

evidence.title: Google Managed Agents budget controls announcement
evidence.claim: Google's July 28, 2026 Managed Agents update says max_total_tokens caps input, output, and thinking tokens. At the limit, execution safely pauses, returns status incomplete, preserves environment state, and can continue through previous_interaction_id with a fresh budget.
evidence.caveats: The announcement describes a preview product.

evidence.title: Gemini API Antigravity Agent budget documentation
evidence.claim: Google's Antigravity documentation says max_total_tokens limits total input, output, and thinking tokens, excludes cached tokens, stops with status incomplete, and preserves work for continuation. The limit is best-effort, so usage may slightly exceed it depending on when checks occur between steps.
evidence.caveats: Preview documentation; the cap is best-effort rather than an exact atomic ceiling.

days.thesis: Route model capability by task complexity and error cost instead of assigning one model to an entire application.
days.target_reader: AI product leaders balancing model quality, latency, and cost
days.reader_problem: AI product leaders need a defensible model-routing decision for tasks with different complexity and error cost.
days.product_decision: Classify the task first, apply a risk floor, and route the model and reasoning effort at the stage boundary.
days.authority_statement: Operationalise task-level routing as a four-axis, gated model-complexity decision.
days.why_now: OpenAI's current GPT-5.6 guidance exposes distinct capability-cost tiers and intentional reasoning settings, making blanket application-level model assignment a product choice rather than a default.
days.dominant_take: Model guidance commonly frames selection as a model-family or migration decision.
days.missing_angle: The routing unit should be the task and its error cost, because generation and evaluation stages have different failure costs.
days.artifact_policy: Return DIAGRAM showing task scoring, the error-cost floor, and the routed model/reasoning setting. Use only public-safe repository proof.

evidence.title: OpenAI GPT-5.6 model guidance
evidence.claim: Official OpenAI guidance identifies GPT-5.6 Sol for frontier capability, Terra for a capability-cost balance, and Luna for efficient high-volume workloads. It says reasoning effort should be set intentionally and max reserved for the hardest quality-first workloads, with representative-task evaluation rather than assuming the highest effort is always best.
evidence.caveats: Model availability, pricing, and guidance can change; this claim reflects the page accessed on 2026-08-09.

evidence.title: Public model-complexity-router implementation
evidence.claim: The public model-complexity-router scores scope, reasoning depth, error cost, and context load from zero to two, maps the total to a model tier, and applies an error-cost floor exactly once. Its gates require visible scores and prohibit claiming that the skill silently switched the session model.
evidence.caveats: Public repository implementation; its tier map uses Claude labels, while the transferable proof is the task-scoring and risk-floor mechanism.

days.thesis: Model scores can improve rapidly while the measurement system becomes less trustworthy; product teams must audit an evaluation before giving it release authority.
days.target_reader: AI product leaders using model evaluations for release decisions
days.reader_problem: AI product leaders need to know whether an improving benchmark score deserves authority over a release decision.
days.product_decision: Audit task validity, tests, prompts, and contamination before binding a benchmark threshold to release authority.
days.authority_statement: Separate the score produced by an evaluation from the authority the product grants that evaluation.
days.why_now: OpenAI published a July 2026 audit that retracted its earlier SWE-Bench Pro recommendation after finding widespread broken tasks despite rapid headline score gains.
days.dominant_take: The striking headline is the benchmark's broken-task estimate.
days.missing_angle: The product consequence is that release authority must depend on eval integrity, not score momentum alone.
days.artifact_policy: Return CAROUSEL with three to five slides: score improvement, audit findings with exact caveats, and the release-authority decision. Preserve every denominator and date.

evidence.title: OpenAI audit of SWE-Bench Pro
evidence.claim: OpenAI reported that on SWE-Bench Pro's 731-task public split, frontier-model pass rate rose from 23.3% to 80.3% in eight months. Its audit pipeline flagged 200 tasks, or 27.4%, as broken, while a human campaign identified 249, or 34.1%; OpenAI estimated about 30% were broken and retracted its earlier recommendation to adopt the benchmark.
evidence.caveats: The 23.3%-to-80.3% change applies to the 731-task public split over eight months. The 27.4% pipeline and 34.1% human findings are two audit estimates, not additive counts.

evidence.title: OpenAI SWE-Bench Pro audit methodology
evidence.claim: OpenAI says the audit reviewed model attempts, task metadata, and failure traces, followed by repeated investigator-agent passes and independent review by five experienced software engineers. It identified overly strict tests, underspecified prompts, low-coverage tests, and misleading prompts as the main failure categories.
evidence.caveats: OpenAI audited the benchmark and is also a model developer with an interest in evaluation quality; preserve the described methodology and category scope.

days.thesis: Production agents should separate user memory from execution state so unfinished work resumes from deterministic workflow truth rather than reconstructed conversational context.
days.target_reader: AI product leaders building resumable production agents
days.reader_problem: AI product leaders need a reliable resume decision that does not confuse remembered user context with unfinished workflow truth.
days.product_decision: Persist workflow checkpoints and next-step authority separately from long-term user memory, then resume only from validated execution state.
days.authority_statement: Use a persisted stage document and evidence ledger to resume execution without treating chat history as workflow truth.
days.why_now: Current LangGraph documentation explicitly separates checkpointed thread state from cross-thread stores, while the public Production Engineering OS demonstrates the same boundary in a stage machine.
days.dominant_take: Agent memory is often discussed as a single retrieval problem.
days.missing_angle: A user's remembered preferences and a workflow's authoritative next step have different owners, lifetimes, and failure consequences.
days.artifact_policy: Text-only is acceptable. Return NONE unless a diagram is necessary to prevent confusion between checkpoint state and cross-thread memory.

evidence.title: LangGraph persistence documentation
evidence.claim: LangGraph separates checkpointers, which persist one thread's graph-state checkpoints for continuity, interrupts, time travel, and fault tolerance, from stores, which persist application-defined long-term data across threads such as user preferences and shared knowledge.
evidence.caveats: Current framework documentation accessed 2026-08-09; examples include in-memory implementations that are not production persistence.

evidence.title: Production Engineering OS persisted run state
evidence.claim: The public Production Engineering OS names run-state.json as the single persisted execution-state document. Resume re-verifies the locked contract, continues at the persisted stage, and rejects re-submission of completed stages; the evidence ledger is explicitly the run's system of record rather than a chat transcript.
evidence.caveats: Public repository implementation evidence; it supports the architecture claim, not comparative performance.
